html:
An epidemic that struck Athens in 430 BCE, the second year of the Peloponnesian War, when the whole population of Attica was crowded inside the walls. It came back in 427 BCE. Perhaps a quarter of the people died, Pericles among them.

Thucydides had it, survived, and described its signs so that it could be recognised again. What disease it was is still argued; typhus and typhoid fever are the leading guesses.
